newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-MCNAMARA FIRES NEW SOUTH WALES TOWARDS VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MCNAMARA FIRES NEW SOUTH WALES TOWARDS VICTORY.

text.p: All-rounder Brad McNamara captured four for 13 to thrust New South Wales towards a crushing victory over South Australia in their Sheffield Shield match on Saturday.
At the close on the third day of their four-day game at the Sydney Cricket Ground, South Australia were in deep trouble at 68 for six, still needing 218 more to avoid an innings defeat.
McNamara ripped through the batting after New South Wales declared their first innings at 440 for six -- a lead of 286 over South Australia's first innings of 154.
New South Wales captain and former Australian all-rounder Greg Matthews scored his first century in five years and was 109 not out at the declaration in this day-night match.
He was the third New South Welshman to make a century in the match, following test discard Michael Slater (102) and Kevin Roberts (119).
On the second day in Hobart, Western Australia were seven runs short of a first innings lead over Tasmania but had only two wickets in hand after a slump in the last session.
Western Australia appeared to be cruising towards a significant lead at 210 for one in reply to Tasmania's 314 at Bellerive Oval.
But the loss of five wickets in the final session left the visitors on 308 for eight at the close.
